translationRepairs: In the first year of Yongshi (33 BCE) he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu at the Capital Township of Xinye in Nanyang, with fifteen hundred households.
In the first year of Yongshi (16 BCE) he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu at the Capital Township of Xinye in Nanyang, with fifteen hundred households.
永始元年 falls in Chengdi’s Yongshi era (16 BCE). The original 33 BCE date belongs to the close of Yuandi’s reign, not this enfeoffment.

Once he secretly purchased a maidservant. When his brothers got wind of it, Mang explained: "Rear General Zhu Boyuan has no son. I have heard that this girl's lineage is auspicious for bearing heirs, so I bought her for him."

Once he secretly purchased a maidservant. When his brothers got wind of it, Mang explained: "Rear General Zhu Ziyuan has no son. I have heard that this girl's lineage is auspicious for bearing heirs, so I bought her for him."
The personal name is 硃子元 (Zhu Ziyuan). Boyuan would require 伯元, which is not in the sentence.
Dai Chong of Changle, Jin She, Ji Hong, Yang Bing, and Chen Tang—all famed men of the day—spoke for him, and the emperor came to esteem Mang.
Dai Chong, Lesser Treasurer of Changle, together with Jin She, Ji Hong, Yang Bing, and Chen Tang—all famed men of the day—spoke for him, and the emperor came to esteem Mang.
長樂少府 is Dai Chong’s office, not a native-place ‘of Changle’. The proposed apposition ‘Lesser Treasury of Changle’ names the bureau rather than the officer.
Recalled to Chang'an, Mang tried to visit Xiu; Xiu feigned sickness and shut his door.
When Mang was summoned away, he tried to visit Xiu; Xiu feigned sickness and shut his door.
及莽徵去 records a summons that took Mang away; the Chinese does not name Chang’an in this unit.
A year after his recall Ai died heirless; Fu and Ding were already in their tombs. The grand empress dowager raced to Weiyang that day, seized the seals of office, and sent a flying summons for Mang.

More than a year after Mang returned to the capital, Emperor Ai died without an heir; Grand Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Ding had both already died. The grand empress dowager that same day drove to Weiyang Palace, seized the seals and ribbons, and sent a courier galloping to summon Mang.
歲餘 is more than a year, not a round year; 哀帝, 傅太后, and 丁太后 are titled persons, and 先薨 is prior death rather than a tomb scene.
First a wind in Yizhou prompted a report that outer barbarians beyond the passes had presented white pheasants,
At first he hinted that Yizhou should have the outer barbarians beyond the passes present white pheasants,
風益州令 is to hint or instruct Yizhou to have the barbarians present pheasants, not a meteorological wind prompting a report.
At first a cyclone prompted the Yi prefecture to report that outer barbarians beyond the passes presented white pheasants,
At first he hinted that Yizhou should order the outer barbarians beyond the passes to present white pheasants,
風 is not a cyclone; 益州 is the jurisdiction ordered to have the outer barbarians present white pheasants.
He wore severity and righteous speech; a hint from him brought a orchestrated memorial from his clique; he then wept and declined—duping the dowager above and the crowd below.
He wore severity and righteous speech; a hint from him brought an orchestrated memorial from his clique; he then wept and declined—duping the dowager above and the crowd below.
The original English is ungrammatical: ‘a orchestrated’ must be ‘an orchestrated’.
The Masters' director Xun was told to command him: "You feign illness over the nomination; your post cannot stand empty—come now."
The Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xun was told to command him: "You feign illness over the nomination; your post cannot stand empty—come now."
尚書令 is the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not a ‘Masters’ director’.

The empress dowager ordered Director of the Masters of Reading Xun to summon him with an edict: "You decline on the excuse of selection; your burden is heavy and may not be vacant; rise at once for the appointed time."

The empress dowager ordered Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xun to summon him with an edict: "You decline on the excuse of selection; your burden is heavy and may not be vacant; rise at once for the appointed time."
尚書令 is not the Masters of Reading; that English office name misrenders the Shangshu directorate.
Wang Shun of Anyang, general of chariots and cavalry, welcomed the prince with merit beyond the passes—add ten thousand households and make him grand guardian.
Marquis of Anyang Wang Shun, general of chariots and cavalry, welcomed the prince of Zhongshan and repelled enemies a myriad li away—add ten thousand households and make him grand guardian.
The original drops 中山王 and flattens 折衝萬里. The proposal still treats 安陽侯 as a place-name ‘of Anyang’ and ‘dashed enemies’ is an awkward rendering of 折衝.

Mang received the titles grand tutor and Duke Who Pacifies Han, declined returning the added fief, adjusted noble rank, and fief matters, saying he wished to wait until the hundred surnames each had enough at home, then receive added reward.

Mang received the titles grand tutor and Duke Who Pacifies Han, declined and returned the added fief and the adjustment of noble rank and fief, saying he wished to wait until the hundred surnames each had enough at home, then receive added reward.
讓還益封疇爵邑事 means he declined and gave back the added fief and the rank-and-fief adjustment; ‘declined returning’ reverses the action.
He also sent Wang Zhaojun's daughter, the Xubu junior chief, to enter and attend.
He also sent Wang Zhaojun's daughter, the Xubu Juci, to enter and attend.
須卜居次 is the Xiongnu title Xubu Juci, not an office ‘junior chief’ held by the daughter herself.

Mang feared they would compete with his own daughter and immediately reported: "Your servant lacks virtue; his son's talents are low. It is not fitting that she be gathered together with the host of girls."

Mang feared they would compete with his own daughter and immediately reported: "Your servant lacks virtue; his child's talents are low. It is not fitting that she be gathered together with the host of girls."
In this memorial 子材下 refers to Mang’s child listed among the girls (與眾女並采), not a son.
Mang asked: "I beg to see the girl."
The dukes and ministers contended: "It is not fitting to gather the other girls and thereby split the legitimate line."
公卿爭曰 introduces the ministers’ objection; the original copies Mang’s later request 願見女 from s0152.
Mang reported: "We beg to see the girl."
The dukes and ministers contended: It is not fitting to gather the various girls and thereby make a second orthodox line.
The speakers are 公卿, not Mang, and the quoted objection is 不宜采諸女以貳正統, not a request to see the girl.
Ministers said: "The queen's bride-gifts barely exceed the concubines' by a little."
Ministers said: "The empress's bride-gifts barely exceed the concubines' by a little."
皇后 is the Han empress; ‘queen’ under-ranks the title in this betrothal context.
It opened with Mang's youth amid Wang luxury, yet choosing thrift and ritual against the tide;
It opened with the Duke Who Pacifies Han from his first coming of age amid an age of extravagance, favored by the two palaces and his uncles, yet choosing thrift and ritual against the tide;
兩宮 is the two palaces, not ‘Wang luxury’; the opening also names 安漢公, 束脩, and 諸父, which the original recasts or omits.
Emperor Ai saw Dong Hong invent dual lineages—Mang impeached him and set the record straight.
When Emperor Ai acceded, Marquis of Gaochang Dong Hong, currying favor, invented dual legitimacies; the Duke personally impeached him and thereby fixed the great ordinances.
孝哀即位 dates the episode to Ai’s accession; 高昌侯董宏 and 公手劾 are omitted or distorted by ‘saw’.
He barred Lady Fu from the imperial dais to preserve protocol.
He submitted that the Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao ought not occupy the imperial curtained seat, thereby making the state's form clear.
The object is 定陶太后, not ‘Lady Fu’; 建白 and 乘輿幄坐 are a memorial about the imperial curtained seat.

Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao wished to establish a presumptuous title; she dreaded the face-to-face rebuke of the curtained-seat righteousness; the bravado of flatterers, the likes of Zhu Bo, punished by the long and Hong impeachments—above and below one heart, slanderous villains crossed in confusion, crooked systems followed, until usurping titles were achieved, benevolent worthies were driven off, affinal kin were slaughtered, while the Duke suffered the complaint of Xu and Yuan, went far to his state, court government collapsed, cords and statutes were cast aside, and the peril of ruin hung no thicker than a hair.

Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao wished to establish a presumptuous title; she dreaded the face-to-face rebuke of the curtained-seat righteousness; the bravado of flatterers, the likes of Zhu Bo, chastened by the impeachments of Chang and Hong—above and below one heart, slanderous villains crossed in confusion, crooked systems followed, until usurping titles were achieved, benevolent worthies were driven off, affinal kin were slaughtered, while the Duke suffered the complaint of Xu and Yuan, went far to his state, court government collapsed, cords and statutes were cast aside, and the peril of ruin hung no thicker than a hair.
長、宏 are the names Chang and Hong, not the adjective ‘long’ paired with Hong.
It paints a nightmare: Dong Xian and Fu kin forging wills and purging Zhongshan—had Mang not returned, coup was certain.

At that time offices lacked a stored heir; Dong Xian held heavy power, and the Fu further had a daughter's support. All knew themselves guilty toward the realm and bound in enmity to Zhongshan; they would surely share one worry, join as if breaking metal, borrow forged testamentary edicts, apply rewards and executions in turn, first removing those they feared and urgently drawing in those they leaned on, then falsely charging old wrongs and further punishing distant kin—once the situation lay open, nothing would have been difficult.
The original invents a ‘nightmare’ and ‘coup’ summary and drops 官亡儲主, 傅氏有女之援, and the forged-edict sequence.
The 《Documents》 says, 'Shun yielded to one whose virtue did not succeed him'—this speaks of the Duke.
The 《Documents》 says, 'Shun yielded on account of virtue and did not succeed'—this speaks of the Duke.
舜讓於德不嗣 is Shun yielding on account of virtue and not taking the succession, not yielding to a person whose virtue failed. The proposal’s bracketed ‘[force]’ is an interpolation.
Like Yu's dark jade and the Duke of Zhou's sacrifice to heaven, he claims no credit that belongs to the skies.
Therefore Bo Yu received the black jade tablet and the Duke of Zhou received suburban sacrifice, for they were heaven's envoys and did not dare monopolize heaven's merit.
伯禹 is Bo Yu; he received the 玄圭, the Duke of Zhou received 郊祀, and the point is 不敢擅天之功.
Gaozu never tired of rewarding a single good word—even a lowly guard who spoke for Fan Kuai won two thousand households.

Gaozu never tired of rewarding a single good word—therefore Gongsun Rong, though only an attendant drawn from the plume-headed guard, for one clear word about Fan Kuai received two thousand households.
The named attendant is 公孫戎; collapsing him into an unnamed ‘lowly guard’ erases the person the Chinese identifies.
Xuandi fattened Huo Guang's fief and spread titles through his nephews.
Xuandi increased Huo Guang's households and spread titles through his elder brothers' grandsons.
兄孫 is grandsons of elder brothers, not nephews; 增戶命疇 is increasing households and granting rank, not ‘fattening’ a fief.
Zhou Bo leaned on kinship armies and a sordid coup—hardly a clean precedent.
Zhou Bo relied on the solidity of Han's feudatories, the stubbornness of Zhuxu, the relays of the generals, and mutual support—though the affair was ugly, in the end it could not succeed.
The original erases 朱虛, invents ‘kinship armies’ and a completed coup, and ignores 其事雖醜，要不能遂.
Mang memorialized: "Yu was misled by Lu Kuan and others, spread rumors and confused the multitude, and shares guilt with Guan and Cai. Your servant dared not conceal this, and begs execution."
Mang memorialized: "Yu was misled by Lü Kuan and others, spread rumors and confused the multitude, and shares guilt with Guan and Cai. Your servant dared not conceal this, and begs execution."
呂寬 is Lü Kuan; Lu Kuan misspells the surname 呂.
Mang used the case to wipe out the Wei, implicate every critic, and drive Princess Jingwu, two princes Li, and Wang Ren to suicide.

Mang used the case to wipe out the Wei, exhaustively try Lü Kuan's case, implicate regional stalwarts who had long criticized him, and drive Princess Jingwu, Liang prince Li, the Marquis of Hongyang Li, and the Marquis of Ping'e Ren to suicide.
梁王立 and 紅陽侯立 are a prince and a marquis both named Li, and 平阿侯仁 is a marquis. The proposal still omits 連引郡國豪桀素非議已者.

And more than eight thousand commoners who submitted memorials all said: yiyin day was made Ah Heng, the Duke of Zhou was made grand steward; the Duke of Zhou enjoyed enfeoffments for seven sons, receiving reward surpassing the supreme duke.

And more than eight thousand commoners who submitted memorials all said: Yi Yin was made Aheng, the Duke of Zhou was made grand steward; the Duke of Zhou enjoyed enfeoffments for seven sons, receiving reward surpassing the supreme duke.
伊尹 is the minister Yi Yin, not a ‘yiyin day’.

The memorial was handed to the responsible officials; they requested returning the two counties earlier added plus Huangyou cluster and Xinye fields, adopting yiyin day and the Duke of Zhou's titles, adding to the Duke the title Regulator-and-Balance, rank above the supreme duke.

The memorial was handed to the responsible officials; they requested returning the two counties earlier added plus Huangyou cluster and Xinye fields, adopting Yi Yin’s and the Duke of Zhou’s titles, adding to the Duke the title Regulator-and-Balance, rank above the supreme duke.
采伊尹、周公稱號 means adopting Yi Yin’s and the Duke of Zhou’s titles, not a ‘yiyin day’.
When the Three Dukes speak on affairs they shall say 'We presume to speak.
When the Three Dukes speak on affairs they shall say 'We presume to speak.'
The quoted formula 敢言之 is left unclosed in the original English.
Let Mang return the extra land he promised for moral example.

The fields at Huangyou, Zhaoling, and Xinye that were yielded in are especially many and all remain with the Duke; the Duke wishes to reduce himself to complete the state’s transformation—it is fitting to grant permission.
The named fields are 黃郵、召陵、新野; the officials ask that the Duke’s wish to reduce himself be granted, not that extra land be forced back as a moral example.
Thirty-six imperial descendants named Xin became marquises; others got bumps in rank or gold.

When the rites finished, Xin and thirty-five other great-great-grandsons of Emperor Xiaoxuan, thirty-six men, were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, with gold and silk rewards each according to number.
孝宣曾孫信第三十六人 names Xin as the first of thirty-six great-great-grandsons, not thirty-six men who all bore the name Xin.

When the rites finished, thirty-six of Xiaoxuan's great-great-grandsons bearing the name Xin were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, gold and silk rewards each according to number.

When the rites finished, Xin and thirty-five others among Xiaoxuan's great-great-grandsons, thirty-six men, were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, gold and silk rewards each according to number.
信第三十六人 is a count headed by Xin, not a statement that each of the thirty-six bore that name.
no ministers surpassed yiyin day and the Duke of Zhou—yet Mang is paired with them.
no ministers surpassed Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—yet Mang is paired with them.
伊、周 are Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; ‘yiyin day’ is a garbled fusion, not a calendar day.
That fall Mang cut the Ziwu road through the mountains, citing the queen's pregnancy omen.
That autumn, because the empress had an auspice of offspring, Mang opened the Ziwu road.
皇后 is the empress; 子孫瑞 is an auspice of offspring, and 通子午道 is opening the Ziwu road, not cutting mountains on a ‘queen’s pregnancy omen’.
The forged Qiang reply listed every miracle—giant grain, self-grown crops, phoenixes, sweet dew—

When asked why Liangyuan submitted, they answered that the grand empress dowager was sage-bright and the Duke Who Pacifies Han supremely benevolent, listing bumper harvests, unsown crops, sweet dew, phoenixes, and divine sparrows.
This unit is Liangyuan’s reported reply praising the grand empress dowager and the Duke; the original invents ‘forged’ and drops the named speakers.
Mang copied King Wu's metal coffer rite, offering his life for the boy's at Tai.
When Emperor Ping fell ill, Mang composed a document, begged for Ping's life at the Grand Suburban Altar, wore the jade disk and held the tablet, and wished to substitute his own body.
This unit has 作策 and 請命於泰畤, not King Wu or a metal coffer. The proposal’s ‘casket document’ borrows 金滕 from the next sentence.
He imposed three years' mourning on every official above six hundred bushels.
Mang summoned ritual experts such as Director of the imperial clan Feng and with them ordered that officials of six hundred bushels and above observe three years' mourning.
莽徵明禮者宗伯鳳等 names the ritualist Feng; the original omits him and turns ‘six hundred bushels and above’ into ‘above six hundred’.
He picked the two-year-old Ying of Guangqi on forged omens.
He therefore chose the youngest of the great-great-grandsons, Ying, son of the Marquis of Guangqi, aged two, claiming that divination and physiognomy showed him most auspicious.
託以為卜相最吉 claims auspicious divination and physiognomy; the Chinese does not say the omens were forged.

In the first month of the first year of acting regency, Mang sacrificed to High God at the southern suburb, welcomed spring at the eastern suburb, performed the great archery rite at the Bright Hall, nourished the three elders and five more-with-completed rites he departed.

In the first month of the first year of acting regency, Mang sacrificed to High God at the southern suburb, welcomed spring at the eastern suburb, performed the great archery rite at the Bright Hall, and nourished the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men; when the rites were complete he departed.
三老五更 is the pair of honorifics Three Elders and Five Experienced Men; 成禮而去 is a separate clause, not ‘five more-with-completed rites’.
None of those under heaven who condemned him dared be first to rise; this is the imperial house's shame.
The original slogan omits 天下非之者乃莫敢先舉. The proposal restores the sense but is ungrammatical English.
A hundred men struck Wan and failed.
Shao and his followers, more than a hundred, advanced to attack Wan, could not enter, and were defeated.
紹等從者百餘人 makes Zhang Shao and his followers the subject, not an unnamed hundred men.
Between Jianping and Yuanshou Han nearly fell,
Between Jianping and Yuanshou the great succession nearly snapped,
元壽 is the era Yuanshou, not ‘Yuanshou Han’; 大統幾絕 is the great succession nearly snapping.
fighting beats flattery, but memorials beat fighting."
